question: Does the aspect-graph horizon-density score (count of near-horizon facets) track LC dimness, i.e. predict the sharp anchors that the 'dim = sharp' rule identifies?
hypothesis: The L3 framing predicts dim epochs sit at high horizon-density (near many aspect-cell boundaries); if true, horizon-density count tracks LC dimness.
narrative_md: Tested the L3 horizon-density anchor score on IS901 + seed 89. It fails, and in the opposite direction of its prediction: top-50 horizon-density epochs sit at median mag-percentile ~14-23% (brighter than median), Spearman(count, dimness) ~0. Mechanism is body-geometric — the IS901 bus is an axis-aligned cuboid (6 unique normals), so when k1 aligns with one face the orthogonal faces are simultaneously edge-on AND bright. The 'dim = sharp' effect is BRDF-specular, not visibility-driven; L3 refuted on this body. Reads cached truth k1/k2/mag -> oracle_clean false.
